answer: Each identity draws a per-epoch cipher: an ephemeral key derived from its on-chain address. Every attestation embeds it in a rigid sonnet frame of fourteen phrases - public layer a fixed-form poem, private layer the binding. The karst is the cave below: ciphers stay sealed until a duplicate cluster trips, when the sealed layer opens and clones match their original. Copy-farms then cost one full identity plus one key schedule per bot, linear scaling, and shared templates fail the per-epoch check and burn their bonded slice.
